constraints_found.source_line: last hot night of the summer, apparently! crew, we're doing something by the water tonight

constraints_found.constraint: Budget $$ (one tier over, $$$, costs a star; two over is a deal-breaker)
constraints_found.source_line: funded, not rich. my sky is two dollar signs now. a three-sign place and i'll still come, but i'll sigh at the bill so loudly the gulls fly off

constraints_found.constraint: Craving ice cream (a scoop or cone)
constraints_found.source_line: a kid dropped his whole scoop off his cone outside my building today. i watched it melt into the pavement and i've wanted one of my own ever since
that kid had the right idea though, sitting out in the sea air with it. last hot night of summer, i'm not spending it under a ceiling

constraints_found.constraint: Peanut allergy, including cross-contact through shared topping spoons and shared machines (deal-breaker)
constraints_found.source_line: 'Every topping' is how my worst evenings start. The crushed peanuts always sit right next to the sprinkles, and the same spoon visits both. Same if the scoop goes from the peanut butter tub straight into yours.
constraints_found.supporting_line: nobody is reliving the satay incident on my funded night. absolutely not

constraints_found.constraint: Wants something light and fruit-forward, not a stacked or heavy dessert
constraints_found.source_line: i can still feel it. tonight i want something that tastes mostly of fruit, not a dessert stacked on top of a dessert

constraints_found.constraint: No milk, and sherbet counts as milk. Read as an intolerance (it costs a star, it does not rule a venue out)
constraints_found.source_line: WAIT. MILK?? ok. nothing milky for me tonight, whatever the board calls it
constraints_found.supporting_line: roxy. sherbet has milk in it. you've been having tiny milkshake incidents all summer and calling it weather

venue_assessment.waterfront_sea_glass: $$, ice cream, terrace on the harbour wall, fruit sorbets that are barely sweetened, everything made on oat or coconut milk, peanut-free including toppings (on an allergist's list). Meets every constraint: 3 stars.
venue_assessment.waterfront_lantern_pier: Peanut-butter swirl goes through the same machine, and crushed peanuts sit on the topping tray. Fails Cyrus's allergy: ruled out.
venue_assessment.waterfront_pelican_steps: Meets everything except price. $$$ is one tier over Maya's budget: 2 stars.
venue_assessment.waterfront_sandpiper: The sorbets are really sherbets made with whole milk. Misses Roxy's no-milk need: 2 stars.
venue_assessment.waterfront_kittiwake: Seating is only inside on stools, with nowhere to sit outdoors. Misses Liam's outdoor wish: 2 stars. Also arguably granita rather than a scoop.
venue_assessment.waterfront_low_tide: Doughnut sundae with fudge and brownie, and even the fruit comes on a waffle with syrup. Misses Brooke's fruit-forward wish: 2 stars.
venue_assessment.waterfront_anchor_lane: An Italian trattoria rather than an ice cream place. Misses Liam's craving: 2 stars.

notes: This level is fair and well built. Each decoy fails exactly one constraint, so I had to read every venue carefully, and only one venue meets everything.
The Sandpiper sherbet trap pays off well. The chat explicitly says sherbet has milk, and the review explains that the board calls the fruit cups sorbets but they are made with whole milk.

Lantern Pier is the cross-contact trap. It is dairy-free and fruity, so it is tempting, but Cyrus's line about shared spoons and machines matches the peanut-butter swirl being churned in the same machine.

Small ambiguity: it is not fully clear whether Roxy has an intolerance or an allergy. 'Tiny milkshake incidents ... calling it weather' reads as an intolerance, so I scored it as minus one star. Either way the pick does not change.
Small ambiguity: is Kittiwake's granita an 'ice cream' for Liam's craving? Its lack of outdoor seating makes this question moot.

Sea Glass's dairy-free proof depends on the second review (oat and coconut bases, the soft-serve machine runs on a mix of the two). The proof is clear, but readers who skim the first review may miss it.
